content:
At the ongoing Formal Conjectures conference, a group of us are working on formalizing the statement of the Hodge Conjecture. @Paul Lezeau will hopefully have a draft of the formalization to share later this week.

We are looking for algebraic geometers to help review the statement to ensure it is correct. If you would like to be included in this project, please reply to this thread!

Thanks for taking this on!
I would be very happy to help review the statement.

Here's a link to the repo: https://github.com/Paul-Lez/HodgeConjecture we're working in (currently we're working on cleaning up the code that was generated, adding sanity checks, checking definitions and so on)
In case it is useful, here is the "trust closure" of HodgeConjecture modulo mathlib. The index is generated from a github action run on my fork of the repo.
This is super cool, thanks for creating this!
If you're happy to open a PR to the main repo to add that, I think this is very useful!
(one small feature request: would it be easy to add a zoom/unzoom feature to help navigate the graph?)

Paul Lezeau said:

(one small feature request: would it be easy to add a zoom/unzoom feature to help navigate the graph?)

There is a zoom scroll handle in the top right, does that do what you want?
Indeed I had missed that - that solved it:)
For people are are interested in helping out on the Hodge conjecture formalisation work, I’ll share a list of tasks that could be worked on shortly
19 messages were moved from this topic to #Formal conjectures > Trust and tools for trust by Johan Commelin.
